title: Gongfu tea pour
summary: Gongfu brewing is a way of making oolong tea with a small clay pot packed with leaves and many very short steeps. The water is poured in a slow circle, the pot is emptied at once into a pitcher, and the tea is shared out so every small cup tastes the same.
howToPlay: Press and circle your finger around the pot to pour hot water evenly over the leaves. Let go when the water reaches the brim.
Watch the steep bar. When the marker enters the green zone, press and hold to pour the tea out.
Keep holding until the last drops have left the pot and are in the pitcher.
Press the pitcher and slide it back and forth over the cups so every cup fills to the dashed line, all alike.
rules: The leaves are rinsed first and that first water is poured away.
There are three infusions, and each steep is a little longer than the one before as the leaves open.
Each pour fills the pot in one even circle up to the brim without spilling over.
The pot is emptied in one clean pour into the pitcher, then shared across four cups.
Score: steeping time 35, equal cups 35, an even circle and brim 15, one clean pour out 10, a dry tray 5.
heritageNote: Gongfu brewing is kept alive in homes and tea houses of southern China, especially the Chaozhou and Fujian regions, and in Taiwan. Its small clay pots, tiny cups and bamboo tea trays are made and handed down by families of potters and tea makers.
